welcomeMessage.en: Today, we are diving into the topic of friendship and relationships.
welcomeMessage.zh: 今天，我们将深入探讨友谊和人际关系的话题。

welcomeMessage.en: We'll discuss what makes a good friend, how friendships change as we get older, and the importance of trust.
welcomeMessage.zh: 我们将讨论什么造就了真正的好朋友，随着年龄的增长友谊是如何改变的，以及信任的重要性。

welcomeMessage.en: Get ready to share stories about your closest friends and favorite memories together!
welcomeMessage.zh: 准备好分享关于你最亲密的朋友以及你们一起最美好回忆的故事吧！

questionsToThinkAbout.en: Who is your oldest friend? How did you first meet them?
questionsToThinkAbout.zh: 谁是你最老的朋友？你们是怎么认识的？

questionsToThinkAbout.en: In your opinion, what are the three most important qualities of a good friend?
questionsToThinkAbout.zh: 在你看来，一个好朋友最重要的三个品质是什么？

questionsToThinkAbout.en: Have your friendships changed since you graduated from school and started working?
questionsToThinkAbout.zh: 自从你毕业开始工作后，你的友谊发生了改变吗？

questionsToThinkAbout.en: Have you ever had an argument with a close friend? How did you resolve it?
questionsToThinkAbout.zh: 你曾经和一个亲密的朋友发生过争吵吗？你是怎么解决的？

questionsToThinkAbout.en: Is it possible for men and women to be just completely platonic friends? Why or why not?
questionsToThinkAbout.zh: 男人和女人之间有可能仅仅是完全纯洁的（柏拉图式的）朋友吗？为什么有可能或为什么不可能？

vocabulary.definition: To slowly become less close or friendly over time.
vocabulary.example: We used to be best friends in high school, but we drifted apart after going to different universities.
I don't have a lot of friends; I just have a few very close friends.

vocabulary.definition: A friend who you know very well and can completely rely on.
vocabulary.example: She is my close friend, so I trust her with all of my secrets.

vocabulary.definition: A person who is fully grown or developed.
vocabulary.example: Do you think it is easy or hard to make new friends as an adult?

vocabulary.definition: An adult (often used by or to children).
vocabulary.example: A grown-up is a person who is not a child anymore.

vocabulary.definition: A person living next door to or very near to the speaker or person referred to.
vocabulary.example: My next-door neighbor is very friendly and always says hello.

vocabulary.definition: A district, especially one forming a community within a town or city.
vocabulary.translation: 街区 / 社区 / 附近
vocabulary.example: There are a lot of great coffee shops and parks in my neighborhood.

vocabulary.definition: A person with whom one works in a profession or business.
vocabulary.example: After work, I sometimes go out for dinner with my colleagues.

vocabulary.definition: Having or showing tact; careful not to offend or upset other people.
vocabulary.translation: 得体的 / 圆滑的 / 委婉的
vocabulary.example: When telling a friend they made a bad choice, you need to be very tactful so you don't hurt their feelings.

sessionSummary: Today's class was a very happy and simple conversation about the people we love and trust: our friends! We answered some deep dive questions about our best friends, how often we see them, and what we do for fun.

We discussed the challenges of making friends as we get older. Everyone shared their thoughts on whether it is easy or hard to make new friends as an adult. We realized that sometimes we drift apart from our childhood friends, but we can always make new connections with neighbors or colleagues at work.

We also learned some important communication skills, like how to be tactful when giving advice to a close friend. Finally, we prepared a fun roleplay and some great homework questions to think about for next time!

grammarTips.title: Grammar Structure: 'It is [adjective] to [verb]'
grammarTips.description: In English, it is very natural to start a sentence with 'It is' when describing an action. This is called a 'dummy subject'. Use this structure instead of putting the verb at the beginning of the sentence.
grammarTips.incorrect: "Make new friends as an adult is hard."
grammarTips.correct: "IT IS hard TO make new friends as an adult. / IT IS wonderful TO see you!"

grammarTips.title: Adult vs. Grown-up
grammarTips.description: These two words mean the exact same thing (a person who is no longer a child). 'Adult' is more formal and common in writing. 'Grown-up' is slightly more casual and is often used by children or when talking to children.
grammarTips.correct: "When I become a grown-up, I want to be a doctor! / Ticket prices are $10 for adults."

grammarTips.title: Spelling Check: Neighbor
grammarTips.description: Be careful with the spelling of 'neighbor'! (It is spelled 'neighbour' in British English and 'neighbor' in American English, but never 'neighber').

homeworkQuestions.title: Homework Questions for Next Class
homeworkQuestions.description: Please think about these questions and be ready to discuss them in our next session:
questions: Giving Advice: If your friend makes a bad choice, do you tell them they are wrong, or do you stay quiet?
Online Friends: Do you have friends that you only talk to on the internet? Do you think internet friends are 'real' friends?

homeworkRoleplay.title: Day 12 Homework: Fun Roleplay
homeworkRoleplay.description: A very simple, happy scenario about seeing an old friend.
homeworkRoleplay.scenario: Imagine I am your old friend. We have not seen each other for five years! We just saw each other on the street.

roles.Step 1: Say hello: Say hi loudly and tell me you are surprised and happy to see me!
roles.Step 2: Ask questions: Ask me how I am doing and what my job is now.
roles.Step 3: Make a plan: Ask me to get coffee or lunch with you next week to catch up.

homeworkRoleplay.preparationTip: Try using the structure 'It is wonderful to see you!' during your roleplay.

goals: Help students correctly use 'It is [adjective] to [verb]'.
Practice using 'tactful' when talking about giving advice.

phases.title: Phase 1: Old Friends (15-20 Minutes)
phases.description: Discuss childhood friends and how relationships change over time.
questions: Who is your oldest friend? How did you first meet them?
Have your friendships changed since you graduated from school and started working?

phases.title: Phase 2: Making New Friends (20-30 Minutes)
phases.description: Talk about the difficulty of making friends as adults.
questions: Do you think it is easy or hard to make new friends as an adult?
How can you be tactful when giving a friend bad news?

phases.title: Phase 3: Fun Roleplay (5-10 Minutes)
phases.description: A very simple, happy scenario about seeing an old friend.
